scenes.shot: about.html, top of the page, cursor still
scenes.text: Your pipeline may be peeking at the future, and STRATA shows you where. Coding agents now write whole pipelines over time-stamped data. The code runs, the score looks good, and the model can still use facts that appeared after the prediction time. STRATA runs the code on the data as it is and on the data as it was at time t, and reports where the two disagree.

scenes.shot: click Open the demo; workbench with feature_program.py, nothing run yet
scenes.text: This is the workbench. On the left, a feature program that a code model wrote for the Olist marketplace. On the right, the diagnosis and a console. Every console output is a recorded strata run on the real data.

scenes.shot: click Run check; wait for LEAK; cursor over the witness table, then over the highlighted lines
scenes.text: Run check. The verdict is leak. The witness names the time, the product, the column, both values, and the table the difference came from: reviews. The program cuts orders at t, but joins every review, including reviews written later.

scenes.shot: click Apply fix; editor jumps to the green lines; click Run check; wait for CLEAN
scenes.text: The suggested fix cuts reviews at their creation date. Apply it and run again. Clean at every tested time, for the witness run, for the canary with a rewritten future, and for the unknown-column probe.

scenes.shot: pick example 'Features that drop cancelled orders'; Run check; wait for UNCHECKABLE
scenes.text: A second program drops cancelled orders. Olist keeps only the latest status, so the status at time t cannot be rebuilt from the data. STRATA answers uncheckable and lists the output columns that depend on it.

scenes.shot: click Schema; click 'With the LLM agent'; click the orders table; cursor on the reason
scenes.text: Where does STRATA know this from? From the availability schema, drafted from the raw files. With the LLM agent, every decision comes with a reason, and the order status is marked as a snapshot that is valid only at the end of the data.

scenes.shot: close; database RelBench F1, example 'Agent-written training script'; Run check; cursor on the top bars of the chart, then on the AUC row
scenes.text: The model layer. An agent-written training script for RelBench Formula One, run exactly as it is, with and without the four hundred and twelve race results that came after t. Predictions move by up to zero point eight seven, and the AUC jumps from zero point seven one to zero point nine three. The metric alone would have missed this.

scenes.shot: database RelBench Event, example 'turns user IDs into numbers'; Run check; cursor on the red cells
scenes.text: The agent layer replaces every ID with a made-up one, twice. This script turns the IDs into numbers, so the two renamings disagree with each other. The output depends on the spelling of the ID, identity recall cannot be separated from that, and the answer is uncheckable.

scenes.shot: database Shop, example 'A prediction table with customers who do not exist yet'; Run check; cursor on the red dates
scenes.text: The task table itself can leak. These three rows predict customers who only sign up later, and STRATA names each one.

scenes.shot: click What is STRATA?; scroll to the results table; click Download SKILL.md; toast appears
scenes.text: On eight databases with known answers, STRATA catches all forty-three leaking code changes and flags none of the fifty-five harmless ones. Download the skill file, and your coding agent runs the check before it reports a score.
